summary: Fresh-agent review of the generated devbook: per-chapter accuracy re-derivation + cross-cutting consistency sweep, before integration
logs: Fresh review: 30 per-chapter reviewers + 4 consistency dimensions.
Reviewed 30 chapters: 17 sign-off, 13 with reservations (2 blocking, 8 major). 4/4 consistency dimensions flagged issues.

issues.fix: Drop the 'run twice' claim — the LIR optimizer runs ONCE (post-BIR, main.rs:712). Reword to: 'The module's value/pointee types are recomputed after BIR synthesis (main.rs:714-716), and the LIR optimizer runs post-BIR (main.rs:712) so DCE/fold/CSE and drop elaboration see the expanded primitives.'

issues.evidence: tests/fixtures/self_host_lowerer/lir_codegen.gg (5265 lines, a full LIR→C backend: emit_structs, emit_externs, emit_box_allocators_from_lir spelling __gorget_box_alloc_<inner> at :721,:738,:775); also lir.gg:509, lir_lower.gg:3698 (GIR→LIR lowering), lir_ssa.gg:606 (SSA), drop_elab.gg:716. issues.fix: Rewrite the second half of the 'In the self-host' section. The self-host DOES implement the LIR layer (lir.gg / lir_lower.gg / lir_ssa.gg / drop_elab.gg) and a C backend (lir_codegen.gg), so the C-emit symbol-spelling boundary (Rule 4 / the runtime-symbol exception) IS exercised in self-host (lir_codegen.gg spells gorget_* / __gorget_box_alloc_<inner> directly). Also worth noting (since it's directly on-topic for Rule 2): the self-host LIR lowering itself still uses name-prefix tests — lir_lower.gg:244 'name.starts_with("Vector__")', :291 'name.starts_with("Box__")' — which is exactly the litmus-test pattern.

findings.detail: SSA merge-mechanism terminology conflicts between the glossary and Chapter 14. The glossary (appendix-b-glossary.md:63) defines SSA as 'each scalar slot becomes a value assigned exactly once, with φ-nodes at control-flow merges.' But Chapter 14 (14-lir-ssa.md:188-189) deliberately emphasizes the opposite as a load-bearing implementation fact: 'Block parameters, not phi nodes — this is the Cranelift model: params: Vec<(ValueId, LirType)>'. For a HOW-IT-IS-IMPLEMENTED book, the glossary's textbook 'φ-nodes' phrasing directly contradicts the exact distinction Chapter 14 calls out; a reader cross-referencing the two finds them at odds on the merge representation. The source itself blurs the two (src/lir/ssa.rs:264 comment 'a block parameter (phi)', and field block_params alongside incomplete_phis at ssa.rs:111-114), so the concepts are equated internally — but the glossary entry should match the chapter's emphasized framing (e.g. 'block parameters at control-flow merges — the Cranelift model, not LLVM-style φ-nodes').

Chapter 15 (15-drop-elaboration.md:3) says 'scheduled ... by optimize_module in src/lir/optimize.rs:46' (the function's doc-comment/definition line; pub fn optimize_module is at line 47, doc comment at 46). The glossary's :78 is the more precise (it is the scheduling call). Recommend aligning the chapter to the call-site line.

Chapter 11 has a dedicated callout (11-copy-on-write.md:169-184, 'Materialization points — the SIX-vs-SEVEN finding') arguing that BOTH the SEVEN and SIX figures are 'stale as a closed enumeration', that 'The current source does *not* maintain a numbered list of materialization points', and that 'Any doc claiming a fixed count is describing an implementation that no longer exists.' Chapter 13 then asserts the opposite as live fact, twice: 13-ownership-in-ir.md:322 says 'Clones happen only at the seven materialization points (assignment, mutating method, struct/enum init, collection put, return, move transfer, field store)', and 13-ownership-in-ir.md:569 cites 'docs/internals/copy-on-write.md Phase 3 — the seven materialization points, full spec' approvingly. Ch 13's enumerated 'seven' is exactly the stale list Ch 11 debunks (Ch 11:209-214 even documents that the 'field store' entry was unified into the shared ensure_owned_at_consuming_arg helper, and Ch 11:186-208 lists >7 live call sites). Source supports Ch 11: ~33 call sites of the two boundary helpers in src/ir/lowering/ (grep), not a fixed enumeration; internals copy-on-write.md:215 and language-reference.md:2297 are the SEVEN-enumeration docs Ch 11 flags as stale. The two devbook chapters cannot both stand — Ch 13 repeats the figure Ch 11 was written to correct.

findings.detail: Contradictory count/set of BIR canonical ops between the C-backend chapter and the BIR/LIR/structural-guard chapters. Chapter 17 presents the canonical-op set as exactly FIVE ops, three times: 17-c-backend.md:18-19 ('expands the *canonical* LIR ops (HofExpand, CowClone, TraitCall, BoxAlloc, AddressOf)'), :59 ('The five BIR-lowered ops (HofExpand, CowClone, TraitCall, BoxAlloc, AddressOf)'), and :227 ('Canonical ops (HofExpand, CowClone, TraitCall, BoxAlloc, AddressOf)'). Chapter 16 (16-bir.md:54-69) says 'Eleven variants are rejected today' and tables eleven; Chapter 25 (25-structural-guards.md:92) lists the same eleven; Chapter 14 (14-lir-ssa.md:125-128) lists eleven. The validator source confirms eleven arms: src/bir/validate.rs:54-108 rejects SizeOf, EnumInit, EnumCheck, EnumExtract, StructInit, CowClone, TraitCall, HofExpand, AddressOf, BoxAlloc, CollectionCtor. Ch 17's 'five' is not a defensible subset framing because it claims 'The C backend never sees those — its emit_inst treats every one of them as unreachable!' while the cited unreachable arm (src/backend/c_lir/mod.rs:2044-2053) actually lists TEN ops (adds SizeOf, EnumInit, EnumCheck, EnumExtract, StructInit), so Ch 17 contradicts both the other chapters (eleven) and its own cited source arm (ten). A reader cross-referencing Ch 16 and Ch 17 gets two different counts for the same set.

findings.detail: Non-issue worth recording so it is not re-raised: the 'sole production backend' axis is internally consistent across the devbook, not contradictory. Ch 17:3 says 'sole production backend' (echoing CLAUDE.md). Ch 19:7 calls LLVM 'a second backend' (deliberately NOT 'second production backend') and Ch 19:11-15 explicitly self-flags the 'sole production backend' wording elsewhere as 'a doc-vs-doc wording inconsistency worth aligning, not a contradiction in behavior.' Ch 14:381 uses neutral 'The production backend is c_lir; an LLVM backend ships behind GG_BACKEND=llvm', and appendix-a:36 says 'C and LLVM backends.' No chapter claims LLVM is a 'second production backend', so there is no live contradiction; the tension is acknowledged and reconciled. Likewise the lexer-parity axis (Ch 03:155 '601 mismatches at ffd58b65, do not assert green' vs Ch 26:172-178 'hundreds of mismatches ... despite memory recording the lexer as green') is fully consistent — both reject the stale 'green' claim and attribute the gap to missing SkFormat / keyword-set drift. The pipeline order (Ch 01:35-78, Ch 14:306-323, Ch 16:302-329) matches src/main.rs:654-717 (pre-BIR compute-types → from_lir → split_critical_edges → optimize POST-BIR → recompute-types) across all three chapters.

Cross-chapter contradiction on the number of production backends. Ch.17 line 3 asserts as bald fact: "The C backend is the sole production backend". But Ch.19 (lines 7-15) describes the LLVM backend as a shipped second backend "held at parity with the C backend ... against the full integration fixture set" and explicitly flags the exact "sole production backend" wording as a doc-vs-doc inconsistency "worth aligning". CLAUDE.md:29-33 confirms the full integration suite is run under GG_BACKEND=llvm with backends "at parity", and src/main.rs:1089 has a real compile_llvm_pipeline. So there is a genuine second, full-suite-tested production codegen path. Ch.17 repeats the disputed phrasing without the qualifier that Ch.19 says it needs — a reader of Ch.17 alone is told there is one production backend; a reader of Ch.19 is told that claim is stale. The two chapters should agree (e.g. Ch.17 should say "the default/primary production backend" or carry the same alignment note Ch.19 does).
